comments.body:
Implementation detail (verified 2026-09-07 in a scratch worktree at origin/main 4c77d6f3e96f; `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, and the complexity ratchet all clean on the edited script):

```diff
@@ -182,12 +182,14 @@ def _run_update_stale(repo_root: Path) -> int:
         print(f"error: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
         return 1
     current = census(repo_root)
-    counters = compare(current, baseline)
-    if counters.has_regression:
+    code, lines = evaluate(current, baseline, markers_for(repo_root))
+    if code != 0:
         print(
-            f"refusing to update: the tree has new/increased mechanisms ({counters.summary})",
+            "refusing to update: the tree has an unadmitted new/increased mechanism",
             file=sys.stderr,
         )
+        for line in lines:
+            print(line, file=sys.stderr)
         return 1
     drained = drain_stale(current, baseline)
     atomic_write(path, render_baseline(drained))
```

Evidence on the committed tree: unfixed script `--update-stale` exits 1 with `refusing to update: the tree has new/increased mechanisms (active=682 new=7 increased=0 stale=0)`; fixed script exits 0, prints `active=682 new=7 increased=0 stale=0`, and `git diff --exit-code .github/mechanism-baseline.json` is clean. The seven admitted mechanisms on main today: `autouse_fixture::tests/conftest.py::_one_engine_root`, `ci_gate::.github/workflows/_scanner-integration.yml::Install rebar from the committed lock (dev extra)`, `ci_gate::.github/workflows/_scanner-integration.yml::Run hash-locked scanner integration contracts`, `ci_gate::.github/workflows/terraform-drift.yml::Assert this tree is current with the tracked branch`, `ci_gate::.github/workflows/test.yml::Prove the Windows exclusive leg (named verdicts)`, `ci_gate::scripts/check_terraform_tree_currency.py`, `ci_gate::scripts/check_user_data_size.py`. Scratch regression test (monkeypatched `BASELINE_PATH`, `detect_all`, `markers_for`): fails on the unfixed script at `assert rc == 0`, passes with the fix; the unmarked-refusal companion passes on both. Full `tests/unit/test_mechanism_delta.py` plus the two scratch tests: 35 passed.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem
The mechanism ratchet has two contracts that disagree about markers. The gate and the unit tests honour them: `evaluate()` (`scripts/_mechanism_delta/compare.py:89-101`) partitions new and increased keys into admitted and unadmitted by exact-key `# mechanism-ok:` marker, and `tests/unit/test_mechanism_delta.py:357-364` asserts `set(baseline) | admitted == live`, so a marker-admitted mechanism is deliberately absent from `.github/mechanism-baseline.json`. The drain does not: `_run_update_stale` (`scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py:177-195`) computes `compare(current, baseline)` (`compare.py:45-57`, marker-blind) and refuses whenever `counters.has_regression` is true (`compare.py:34-35`). This is live today: on origin/main 4c77d6f3e96f the committed tree carries seven marker-admitted mechanisms with no baseline row (`--check` reports `active=682 new=7 increased=0 stale=0`, all seven `admitted`), so `--update-stale` refuses on an unmodified checkout (`refusing to update: the tree has new/increased mechanisms`, exit 1; reproduced 2026-09-07 in a scratch worktree). Consequences: (1) any change that removes a censused mechanism leaves a stale row that `test_the_committed_baseline_matches_the_live_tree` rejects, and the only tool that drops the row refuses, so the only way through is the forbidden hand-edit (the wall the agent on Gerrit change 2658 hit, recorded on celadon-computable-smelts a1f1-a30d-2d50-4f5a); (2) this blocks all ten breaking-release stories that delete a mechanism (granitic-realisable-dolphin, anguished-grown-junebug, emblematic-apostolic-mouse, captious-tangled-pigeon, reviewable-infatuated-arcticduck, fuchsia-wettish-leafbird, quilted-nepotic-kitty, masonic-excusable-guppy, valued-canine-darwinsfox, citified-earth-cottontail), so this fix lands before any of them. Operator decision 2026-09-07: the drain in the same change is the sanctioned step for removals, and the marker remains the sanctioned path for additions, so the drain must honour markers exactly as the gate does.

## Approach
Make the drain's refusal the gate's own verdict. In `_run_update_stale`, replace the `compare()` plus `has_regression` refusal with `code, lines = evaluate(current, baseline, markers_for(repo_root))` and refuse (print the report lines to stderr, return 1, baseline byte-identical) when `code != 0`; otherwise `drain_stale(current, baseline)` and write as today. `markers_for` is already defined in the script (`:117`) and `evaluate` is already imported, so no import changes; `compare` stays in use for the final summary print. The exact diff, verified in a scratch worktree, is in this ticket's first comment. `drain_stale` only drops keys, so admitted keys stay out of the baseline and the unit-test invariant `set(baseline) | admitted == live` continues to describe the written file. A blank marker still refuses through `evaluate`'s blank-marker errors. Reword the two prose statements of the old rule: `docs/architecture.md:674-677` becomes "`--update-stale` drops entries whose definition site is gone and rewrites canonical sorted JSON. It refuses to write, leaving the baseline byte-identical, while any UNADMITTED mechanism is new or increased, so it can never bless a regression; a marker-admitted mechanism does not block it. Run it in the same change whenever your change removes a mechanism and `--check` reports only stale rows; a contributor never hand-edits the baseline." `AGENTS.md:389-390` becomes "Do not hand-edit `.github/mechanism-baseline.json`. When your own change removes a mechanism, run `python scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py --update-stale` in that change and commit the shrunken baseline; the drain refuses while any unadmitted mechanism is new or increased, so it cannot bless a regression." Extend the source-level pin at `tests/unit/test_mechanism_delta.py` (about `:480-530`, the test that asserts the two committed-tree tests consult `markers_for`) to also cover `_run_update_stale`, so a wholesale revert cannot silently make the drain marker-blind again (the failure mode recorded on satin-fullgrown-shibainu affd-913c-3fb0-40fb).

## Scope
`scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py` (`_run_update_stale`, the `--update-stale` help text at the parser), `docs/architecture.md` (the drain paragraph), `AGENTS.md` (the mechanism-ratchet paragraph), `tests/unit/test_mechanism_delta.py`. Out of scope: `compare()` and `evaluate()` themselves, the detectors, the complexity ratchet, `.github/mechanism-baseline.json` (unchanged by this fix: with the fix applied, `--update-stale` on the committed tree writes nothing, verified).

## Testing
Red first: new `test_update_stale_drains_while_an_admitted_mechanism_stands` in `tests/unit/test_mechanism_delta.py`, built like `test_update_stale_refuses_to_write_while_a_regression_stands` (`:338-350`): baseline `{"lock::a.lock": 1, "lock::gone.lock": 1}`, `detect_all` monkeypatched to `{"lock": {"a.lock", "marked.lock"}}`, `markers_for` monkeypatched to `{"lock::marked.lock": "bug 1768 - probe"}`; assert `main(["--update-stale"])` returns 0 and the written baseline is exactly `{"lock::a.lock": 1}` (stale row dropped, admitted key not added). This test was run against the unfixed script in the scratch worktree and failed at `assert rc == 0`, and passed with the fix (35 passed with the existing 33). The existing refusal test stays green unchanged (an unmarked `surprise.lock` still refuses, baseline byte-identical). A second new test: a marker whose reason is blank still refuses. The pin test asserts `_run_update_stale`'s AST references `markers_for`. Then `python scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py --check` and `--update-stale` on the committed tree (expected: `new=7` all admitted, exit 0, no write), `make lint`, `make verify`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `--update-stale` writes when the only new or increased mechanisms are marker-admitted, drops the stale rows, and does not add the admitted keys; verified by the new unit test.
- [ ] `--update-stale` still refuses, baseline byte-identical, on an unadmitted new mechanism and on a blank marker; verified by the existing refusal test plus the new blank-marker test.
- [ ] The source-level pin covers `_run_update_stale`; verified by the extended pin test failing when the `markers_for` call is removed (recorded red-then-green in the commit message).
- [ ] `docs/architecture.md` and `AGENTS.md` state the new rule and no longer say `--update-stale` is maintenance-only; verified by `grep -n "maintenance-only" AGENTS.md docs/architecture.md` returning only the complexity-ratchet `--lock` sentence.
- [ ] `make verify` exits 0 and the committed baseline is unchanged (`git diff --exit-code .github/mechanism-baseline.json`).
